claims.text: The as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy has a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
Adding a targeted alloying element can stabilize the non-equilibrium solid solution in an Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy.
Zn, Ca, or Sr are candidate additions for stabilizing the solid solution.
Stabilization of the non-equilibrium solid solution suppresses stable intermetallic formation.
Suppressing stable intermetallic formation improves room-temperature compressive behavior relative to the as-processed baseline.
Suppressing stable intermetallic formation improves corrosion resistance relative to the as-processed baseline.
Suppressing stable intermetallic formation increases resistance to high-temperature oxidation relative to the as-processed baseline.
The modified alloy is intended to retain a density below 6 g/cm3.
